subject: Biology
title: Mutations and Evolution
description: A micro-lesson that makes Mutations and Evolution usable.

hook.text: Evolution can't happen without mutation. It is the only source of brand-new genetic variation.

buildup.text: Most mutations are neutral. Natural selection acts only on those that affect survival.

discovery.text: Beneficial mutations spread slowly through populations over many generations.

twist.text: Lactose tolerance in adults arose from a mutation only about 7,500 years ago in Europe.

climax.text: From antibiotic-resistant bacteria to high-altitude humans, mutations shape adaptation.

punchline.text: Every adaptation started as a lucky typo.

quiz.question: Where does new genetic variation ultimately come from?

details.summary: Mutations are the ultimate source of all genetic variation and thus all evolutionary change. While most mutations are neutral or harmful, rare beneficial mutations provide the raw material that natural selection uses to adapt populations to changing environments.
details.whyItMatters: Without mutation, evolution would be impossible because there would be no new genetic variants for selection to act upon. Understanding mutation rates helps predict evolutionary trajectories and disease emergence.
takeaways: Most mutations are neutral with no effect on fitness or survival
Beneficial mutations are rare but essential for adaptive evolution
Mutation rate itself can evolve under natural selection

faq.question: How often do mutations occur in human DNA?
faq.answer: Each human carries about 60 to 70 new mutations not present in either parent. Most occur in non-coding regions and have no effect. Over generations, this steady input of variation provides material for natural selection to work with.

faq.question: Can natural selection create mutations?
faq.answer: No. Mutations arise randomly regardless of whether they would be beneficial. Natural selection only preserves or eliminates existing mutations. An organism cannot will a useful mutation into existence. Mutation creates variation; selection shapes it.
